prompt: The prose prompt, run with a temperature of 0.8 left in the command, broke 14 messages against the bulleted prompt, with p = 0.001. What does that let you conclude?
hint: How many things changed between the two runs?

choices.text: Prose is worse than bullets, and the evidence is strong
choices.why: The temperature changed too, and the test cannot separate the two.

choices.text: Only that the runs differ
choices.why: Right: two changes, one number.

choices.text: Nothing, because a p that small is suspicious
choices.why: A small p is fine; it just does not name a cause.

choices.text: Bullets only help when the temperature is high
choices.why: Nothing was measured that would show that.

prompt: Which of these is missing from a line of a run file?
hint: Look at `head -n 1 runs/v7-warm.jsonl`.

choices.text: The prompt's id
choices.why: It is there, as `prompt`.

choices.text: The `--set` value
choices.why: Right, so write the command down with the run.

choices.text: The test set the message came from
choices.why: It is there, as `cases`.

choices.text: Why the reply stopped
choices.why: It is there, as `stop`.

prompt: You are testing a new wording of the instructions. What should stay the same between the two runs? Choose all that apply.
hint: Everything except the change.

choices.text: The test set
choices.why: Yes: different messages compare the messages as much as the prompts.

choices.text: The temperature and the other parameters
choices.why: Yes: that is the change that rode along in the first run.

choices.text: The labels and the order they are listed in
choices.why: Yes: they are part of the prompt, and not the change.

choices.text: The prompt's id
choices.why: It is a hash of the file, so any change to the wording changes it.

prompt: Why does `pl compare` line up the two results of each message instead of comparing two totals?
hint: Think of 46 against 48.

choices.text: Totals are rounded, and messages are not
choices.why: Nothing is rounded in a count of passes.

choices.text: It is faster
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Two totals two apart hide how many messages moved, and in which direction
choices.why: Right, and the messages that moved are the evidence.

choices.text: Totals include the messages the model never answered, which would skew them
choices.why: Every message was answered in both runs.

prompt: With the temperature of 0.8 left in, how many messages did the prose prompt break?
hint: The `broken` count in `pl compare`.

prompt: Comparing answers with `--answers`, how many of the seventy categories differed between bullets and prose?
hint: `different answer` in the output.

prompt: Why were `t26` and `t39` counted as fixed under the prose prompt?
hint: Compare `pl show` for `t26` under each prompt.

choices.text: Prose explained their categories more clearly, so the stand-in sorted them correctly at last
choices.why: No category changed; they were right under both.

choices.text: They lost the code fence they had under the bullets
choices.why: Right. The fences moved to other messages.

choices.text: The prose prompt asked for JSON more firmly
choices.why: Both ask for the JSON object alone.

choices.text: Their messages were shorter
choices.why: The messages were identical in both runs.

prompt: In the stand-in, moving one full stop in the prompt changes which replies come back in a code fence. Why?
hint: What is the habit's number rolled from?

choices.text: Full stops count as instructions
choices.why: The stand-in reads no instruction in a full stop.

choices.text: The prompt became longer than the stand-in's limit
choices.why: One character does not reach any limit.

choices.text: The stand-in prefers fences when sentences are long and the prompt reads as prose
choices.why: Its rule has nothing to do with sentence length.

choices.text: Its habits are rolled from a hash of the whole prompt
choices.why: Right: any change to the text reshuffles them.

prompt: What is the honest report of the bullets-against-prose experiment?
hint: Two messages moved, both by formatting.

choices.text: Prose is two points better
choices.why: Two messages are noise here, and the sign test says so.

choices.text: No difference visible in seventy messages
choices.why: Right. Saying so is the result, not a failure.

choices.text: Prose is better at JSON, worse at categories
choices.why: No category changed, and each prompt had two format failures.

choices.text: The experiment failed and has to be repeated at a higher temperature
choices.why: It worked; it found nothing, and a temperature would add a second change.

prompt: A difference of a few messages that the test set cannot tell apart from chance is ___.
hint: What the section calls the two that moved.

prompt: Which messages enter the sign test that `pl compare` prints?
hint: The line says how many.

choices.text: All the messages in the test set
choices.why: Messages with the same result twice say nothing about the difference.

choices.text: Only the messages that failed under both prompts
choices.why: Those say nothing about the difference either.

choices.text: Only those whose result changed
choices.why: Right: fixed plus broken.

choices.text: The messages the second prompt passed
choices.why: Most of those passed under the first as well.

prompt: Every changed message moves in the same direction. What is the smallest number of changed messages for which the sign test gives p below 0.05?
hint: Halve, then double, until it falls under.

prompt: Five changed messages, all fixed and none broken. What p does the sign test give?
hint: Twice a half to the fifth power.

prompt: A change fixes 7 messages and breaks 1, and the sign test gives 0.07. A colleague writes "no effect" in the report. What is wrong with that?
hint: What does a p above 0.05 say?

choices.text: Nothing: above 0.05 proves the change does nothing
choices.why: A p value does not prove the absence of an effect.

choices.text: The sign test ought to be computed over all seventy messages
choices.why: The unchanged ones carry no evidence about the difference.

choices.text: The one broken message cancels the seven fixed ones
choices.why: It raises the bar; it does not cancel them.

choices.text: No effect shown is not no effect
choices.why: Right. A bigger test set might settle it.

prompt: What does p = 0.001 on a comparison tell you?
hint: It is about chance, not about causes.

choices.text: There is a 99.9% chance that the change made the prompt better
choices.why: p is not the probability that the change helped.

choices.text: A split that uneven would be rare if the change did nothing
choices.why: Right, and it says nothing about which change did it.

choices.text: The change affected one message in every thousand it was run on
choices.why: p is not a share of messages.

choices.text: The wording caused the difference
choices.why: In the run with the temperature left in, p was 0.001 and the wording was not shown to matter.

prompt: How many of the lab's tokens did the order cost written as JSON?
hint: The second `pl tokens` line.

prompt: You add a hundred more orders. Why does the table's cost per order fall while JSON's stays about the same?
hint: Where do the field names go in each?

choices.text: A table pays for its header once; JSON repeats every key in every record
choices.why: Right: the header's share falls with every row.

choices.text: JSON values are longer
choices.why: The values are the same in both.

choices.text: Tables are compressed by the tokenizer
choices.why: The lab's tokenizer compresses nothing.

choices.text: Commas are free
choices.why: Each comma is a token in the lab.

prompt: Why can this lab not show you whether the format of the input data changes the answers?
hint: How does the stand-in decide a category?

choices.text: It sorts by keywords, whatever surrounds them
choices.why: Right. A real model is not so indifferent, which is why you measure there.

choices.text: It refuses JSON in the message
choices.why: It reads JSON like any other text.

choices.text: The harness converts every input to prose before the call
choices.why: The harness sends the prompt exactly as rendered.

choices.text: Format only matters at temperature above 0, and the lab runs at 0
choices.why: Temperature has nothing to do with it.

prompt: After finding large accuracy swings from formatting alone, what did Sclar and others (2023) recommend?
hint: One format is one sample.

choices.text: Always format prompts as JSON
choices.why: They did not name a winning format.

choices.text: Stop using few-shot prompts
choices.why: They measured few-shot prompts; they did not ban them.

choices.text: Report performance across a range of plausible formats
choices.why: Right, not on the single format somebody happened to write.

choices.text: Choose the format with the fewest tokens
choices.why: Cost and accuracy are separate questions.

prompt: Put the steps of a wording experiment in order.
hint: From the change to the report.
items: Write down the one change, and the command you will run
Run both prompts on the same test set with the same parameters
Read the sign test and the messages that moved, then report

prompt: Match each result from this lesson to what it meant.
hint: One each.

pairs.right: Too few changes to tell from chance

pairs.left: p = 0.001 with a temperature left in
pairs.right: A real difference with two possible causes
A code fence around a correct answer

prompt: A colleague rewrites the urgency rules and adds a fourth example in the same commit. The score goes from 46 to 51 of 70, with p = 0.06. What do you ask for?
hint: Two changes, and a p near the line.

choices.text: Nothing: five more passes out of seventy is clearly better than before
choices.why: Two changes and a p of 0.06 support neither claim.

choices.text: A run at a higher temperature, to see more variety in the answers before deciding
choices.why: That adds a third change.

choices.text: Each change run on its own against the old prompt, ideally on more messages
choices.why: Right: one change at a time, and a test set big enough to see it.

choices.text: The same run again, to confirm it
choices.why: At temperature 0 the stand-in gives the same answers; it proves nothing new.
